brief: The Market Ear catalogs a run of extreme-low hedge fund positioning readings across metrics, framed as observations rather than a thesis. US long/short net leverage has collapsed to 43.4%, the 0th percentile of its five-year range (Goldman Sachs Prime Brokerage), and the fundamental long/short ratio by market value sits at the same 0th percentile. Global equity long/short net leverage is at the 2nd-3rd percentile (JPMorgan PI). Despite this de-risking, hedge funds were down 3.3% MTD following Thursday's selloff versus a 0.2% S&P 500 gain, so the hedging did not protect performance. The AI trade has also lost its edge: the S&P 500 ex-AI has outperformed the headline index YTD (Goldman Sachs trading desk). Jefferies' desk flow shows heavy Tech selling, over $1B net sold on 7 of the last 10 days and one of its most dramatic 20-day net-selling periods in Tech. The exception is Magnificent Seven exposure, which Morgan Stanley data puts at the 81st/77th percentile, far from washed out. The note explicitly states it draws no conclusions and distrusts the usual contrarian-bullish read of such low positioning.
